question.text: A Category III AIF selling CDS may earmark which securities against the CDS exposure, and what is the treatment for leverage computation?

answer.text: Unencumbered Government bonds/Treasury bills; NOT counted towards leverage limit
Equity shares of unlisted entities; counts towards leverage

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 5.15, sellers of CDS must earmark unencumbered G-secs/T-bills equal to CDS exposure; these earmarked securities are NOT counted for leverage limit computation. The Trap: Corporate bonds or equities are not the permissible earmarking assets; earmarking G-secs actually REDUCES effective leverage counted. Cross-Exam Context: Novel feature introduced in January 2023 — unique to Cat III.
